title: Which Policy Works, and Where? Estimation and Inference for State-Level Treatment Effects in Difference-in-Differences
abstract: arXiv:2609.01467v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Policies with a common objective and implementation date may differ in details or context. We distinguish the aggregate average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) from sub-aggregate ATTs defined by implementation cohort, jurisdiction, period, or policy type. UN-DID and DID-INT, two DiD estimators that construct jurisdiction-by-time effects, estimate these ATTs under parallel-trends conditions matched to the aggregation. In CPS placebo-law simulations, randomization inference is generally well-sized, though some jurisdiction-specific tests are conservative. The jackknife can be undefined for sub-aggregate ATTs; when defined, it over-rejects with few treated or comparison jurisdictions. Estimands and inference methods should match the policy question and implementation setting.

translated_title: 哪项政策有效，在何地有效？双重差分法中州级处理效应的估计与推断
translated_abstract: 具有共同目标和实施日期的政策在细节或实施背景上可能存在差异。我们将总体的平均处理效应（ATT）与按实施批次、司法管辖区、时期或政策类型定义的次总体ATT区分开来。UN-DID和DID-INT是两种构建司法管辖区-时间效应的双重差分估计量，可在与聚合方式相匹配的平行趋势条件下估计这些ATT。在CPS安慰剂法则模拟中，随机化推断通常具有较好的检验水平，尽管某些特定司法管辖区的检验较为保守。刀切法对于次总体ATT可能是无定义的；即使有定义，当处理组或对照组司法管辖区数量较少时，它会过度拒绝原假设。估计对象和推断方法应与政策问题和实施环境相匹配。
tldr: 该论文提出UN-DID和DID-INT两种双重差分估计量，用于估计按实施批次、司法管辖区、时期或政策类型定义的次总体平均处理效应，并强调估计对象与推断方法应与政策问题和实施环境相匹配。
